glass-horizon-exterior.text: RFV Glass Horizon exterior — mature Fleet survey cruiser built for repeated anomaly work rather than line combat: long instrumented hull in deep Fleet blue and Ion White, restrained gold registry marks, fractured-crystal Glass Horizon crest, modular survey pods, sacrificial sensor booms, beacon racks and multiple small-craft bays. Survey-violet light is limited to active instrumentation.

glass-horizon-bridge.text: Glass Horizon bridge — practical wide bridge centered on navigation, pilot, systems and command stations rather than ceremonial display. Deep-blue structure, Ion White work light, restrained gold Fleet markings, tactile route surfaces, redundant physical controls and a broad forward viewport with sensor shutters.

glass-horizon-survey-lab.text: Glass Horizon survey lab — instrument-dense working space with suspended Lattice plots, physical route boards, sample lockers, timing references and redundant sensor feeds. Displays are functional and sparse; crew can point to provenance and compare independent measurements.

glass-horizon-cartography.text: Glass Horizon cartography bay — layered physical and projected maps, route-certification table, beacon-status controls and archive stations. Public-safe lanes are green only after certification; provisional or unsafe paths remain non-green and visibly qualified.

glass-horizon-hangar.text: Glass Horizon survey hangar — compact bay holding Lantern Two, probe racks, tether drones and temporary survey beacons. Equipment is scarred, modular and meant to be replaced after hazardous work.

lantern-two.text: Lantern Two — compact two-seat Fleet survey cutter with pilot and navigator stations, strong inertial recorder, diversified ranging sensors, physical handholds, tether hardpoints and no combat styling beyond basic protective systems.

quiet-route-entry.text: Quiet Route entry — a narrow apparent calm between crystalline Aurin debris fields. Stars seem unusually steady, dust motion dampens near the opening, and temporary survey beacons stand outside the path with public status locked non-green.

quiet-route-interior.text: Quiet Route interior — dark low-tension corridor with sparse crystalline reflections and unusually clean star fields. It looks simpler than surrounding Lattice space, which is precisely what makes the later measurement contradictions unsettling. Geometry can shift under beacon feedback without becoming a kaleidoscope.

beacon-field.text: Temporary Glass Horizon beacon field — six rugged survey beacons spaced through the candidate corridor, each with physical struts, redundant clocks and survey-violet diagnostic light. Their public navigation channel remains red/non-certified; no beacon turns green during Issue 1.
